sprint_note: Wires scheduled task status to CalendarConnector: create all-day event on schedule, update on date/title change, delete on unschedule. Best-effort, non-blocking. No schema change. No frontend change.
summary: Lightweight single-user task management application that creates, tracks, and labels tasks with status, priority, due date, effort, and scheduled time fields, persisting tasks in Postgres and delegating label management to LabelEngine, user preferences to PreferenceStore, and calendar blocking to CalendarConnector.

classification.why_application: Owns task domain state (tasktracker.tasks table), enforces task-specific business rules (status transitions, priority validation, effort constraints, scheduled promotion logic, calendar sync trigger logic), and wires platform services to TaskTracker-scoped behavior. Contains no reusable infrastructure.
non_goals: Reverse calendar sync — changes in Google Calendar do not flow back to Atlas
Frontend changes — all logic in backend only
LinkingEngine integration — task.id is used directly as atlas_event_id
Deep-link route /tasks/:id — planted in event description; route added in Sprint 11
Retry logic for failed calendar sync calls
Background job scheduler — promotion is lazy on page load only
classification.not_platform: Task domain rules, the tasktracker.tasks schema, the wiring of LabelEngine/PreferenceStore/CalendarConnector for this domain, and the calendar sync trigger decisions (when to create/update/delete) are TaskTracker-specific application behavior, not reusable platform infrastructure.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks
exposed_surfaces.purpose: List tasks with optional status or view filter and pagination. Embeds labels per row from LabelEngine batch call. view=active and view=pending_board trigger auto-promotion before SELECT. view=scheduled returns scheduled tasks ordered by scheduled_at ASC.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/tasks
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create a new task. Accepts status=scheduled with required scheduled_at. If status=scheduled, fires best-effort calendar create after DB commit. Returns created task as Dataset (single row).

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/tasks/{task_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Partially update a task. Field omission means no change; explicit null clears nullable fields. After DB commit, fires best-effort calendar create/update/delete based on status transition. Returns updated task as Dataset (single row).

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/tasks/{task_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Delete a task. Returns empty Dataset on success.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/labels/search
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Search labels by name prefix via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/labels/used
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return all labels attached to at least one task. Gracefully degrades to empty Dataset on LabelEngine failure.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return all labels attached to one task via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Attach a label by name to a task via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels/{label_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Detach a label from a task via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: PUT /api/tasks/{task_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Atomically replace all labels on a task via LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/tasks/preferences/label_filter
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Retrieve stored label filter selection from PreferenceStore.

exposed_surfaces.name: PUT /api/tasks/preferences/label_filter
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Persist label filter selection to PreferenceStore.

internal_flow.name: startup_init
internal_flow.description: On FastAPI startup: init_pool() creates psycopg2 SimpleConnectionPool. init_schema() reads schema.sql and executes DDL idempotently. CALENDAR_CONNECTOR_URL and ATLAS_BASE_URL are read from environment at module load. Errors are logged; application continues.
outputs: tasktracker schema and tasks table in Postgres

internal_flow.name: task_list
internal_flow.description: GET /tasks validates params, runs auto-promotion if view=active or view=pending_board, executes the appropriate SELECT, embeds labels via LabelEngine batch POST. Returns Dataset. Unchanged from Sprint09.
outputs: Dataset with task rows and embedded labels

internal_flow.name: task_create
internal_flow.description: POST /tasks validates title, status (open|pending|scheduled), priority, effort_hours, and scheduled_at. Inserts row with UUID. Commits. If status=scheduled, calls _sync_calendar_event(task_id, title, scheduled_at, description, 'create') after commit. Returns Dataset (single row). Calendar failure never propagates to response.

internal_flow.name: task_update
internal_flow.description: PATCH /tasks/{task_id} validates status/priority if provided. Fetches pre-update snapshot (status, scheduled_at, title, description). Builds SET clause from model_fields_set. Executes UPDATE RETURNING *. Commits. Then evaluates calendar action from pre/post state: (a) any→scheduled (new): 'create'; (b) scheduled→scheduled and scheduled_at or title changed: 'update'; (c) scheduled→other: 'delete'; (d) no status change, not scheduled: no-op. Calls _sync_calendar_event as appropriate. Returns Dataset (single row) or 404 ApiError. Calendar failure never propagates.
inputs: pre-update DB snapshot (status, scheduled_at, title, description)

internal_flow.name: task_delete
internal_flow.description: DELETE /tasks/{task_id} executes DELETE RETURNING id. Returns empty Dataset or 404 ApiError. Note: no calendar cleanup on DELETE — the task is gone and CalendarConnector's idempotent delete is not called in this sprint (calendar event orphan risk is accepted as a deferred decision).

internal_flow.name: calendar_sync
internal_flow.description: _sync_calendar_event(task_id, title, scheduled_at, description, action): if CALENDAR_CONNECTOR_URL is empty, returns immediately. Otherwise opens an httpx.Client targeting CALENDAR_CONNECTOR_URL. For 'create': POST /api/calendar/events with {atlas_event_id, title, start_at, end_at, description, all_day=true}. For 'update': PATCH /api/calendar/events/{task_id} with {title, start_at, end_at, description, all_day=true}. For 'delete': DELETE /api/calendar/events/{task_id}. All httpx exceptions and non-2xx responses are caught, logged as warnings, and swallowed. start_at = scheduled_at.isoformat(), end_at = (scheduled_at + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat(). title is prefixed with '[Atlas] '. description = 'Atlas task: {ATLAS_BASE_URL}/tasks/{task_id}\n\n{description or ""}'.
outputs: none (side-effect only; all errors swallowed with log.warning)

internal_flow.name: label_proxy
internal_flow.description: Label endpoints are thin proxies to LabelEngine with object_type=task. Results mapped to Dataset for read endpoints. Unchanged from Sprint09.
inputs: task_id, label_name, or label_id as applicable

internal_flow.name: preference_proxy
internal_flow.description: Preference endpoints are thin proxies to PreferenceStore under scope=tasktracker.task-list. Unchanged from Sprint09.
outputs: Dataset or 404 ApiError (GET) | PreferenceRecord or ApiError (PUT)

deferred_decisions: Calendar cleanup on task DELETE: the current design does not call CalendarConnector DELETE when a task is hard-deleted. The calendar event will become orphaned. This is acceptable for Sprint10; a cleanup strategy can be added in a future sprint if needed.

scheduled_at change detection in PATCH: the 'update' branch requires knowing whether scheduled_at or title actually changed. The pre-update snapshot fetched for status validation already includes scheduled_at and title — implementer must compare pre-snapshot values against the body fields using model_fields_set to determine if an update is warranted.

risks.risk: Calendar event orphan on task DELETE
risks.impact: A deleted task leaves a dangling calendar event in Google. Low impact for single-user; event can be manually removed. Deferred to a future sprint.

risks.risk: CalendarConnector not yet OAuth-authorized at runtime
risks.impact: Calendar sync returns non-2xx (NO_CALENDAR_CONNECTION or INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE). Warning logged, task operation succeeds. User must connect CalendarConnector separately.

risks.risk: PATCH update 'no-op' detection requires comparing pre-snapshot title against body title
risks.impact: If implementer omits this check, spurious PATCH calls to CalendarConnector may occur on every scheduled PATCH. Non-fatal but wasteful. Reviewer should verify.

risks.risk: scheduled_at stored as date in DB (not timestamptz)
risks.impact: All-day events use date-only strings — this matches the CalendarConnector all_day=true expectation. No correctness issue.
